question: 48 + (72 + 16) − 34 × 2 + 19 + 11 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 98.

GIVEN

• 48 + (72 + 16) − 34 × 2 + 19 + 11

SOLUTION

• Brackets first: (72 + 16) = 88

• Multiply: 34 × 2 = 68

• 48 + 88 − 68 + 19 + 11 = 136 − 68 + 30 = 68 + 30 = 98.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Add all the plus-terms first (48 + 88 + 19 + 11 = 166) and subtract the only minus-term (68): 166 − 68 = 98. No need to keep re-scanning the line.

NOTE

• Follow BODMAS: Brackets → Of/Order → Division/Multiplication → Addition/Subtraction, left to right.

question: 99 − 41 + 18 × 2 + (33 ÷ 3) − 22 + 16 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 99.

GIVEN

• 99 − 41 + 18 × 2 + (33 ÷ 3) − 22 + 16

SOLUTION

• Bracket/Division: 33 ÷ 3 = 11

• Multiply: 18 × 2 = 36

• 99 − 41 + 36 + 11 − 22 + 16 = 99 − 41 = 58; 58 + 36 = 94; 94 + 11 = 105; 105 − 22 = 83; 83 + 16 = 99.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Group positives (99 + 36 + 11 + 16 = 162) and negatives (41 + 22 = 63): 162 − 63 = 99.

NOTE

• Resolve brackets and ÷/× before doing +/−; work the additions/subtractions strictly left to right.

question:
The line chart given below shows the number of hours for which the 6 students ST1, ST2, ST3, ST4, ST5 and ST6 study in a month.

For the given 6 students, what is average hours of study per student in the given month?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 122.33.

GIVEN

• Study hours: ST1 = 65, ST2 = 126, ST3 = 135, ST4 = 148, ST5 = 165, ST6 = 95

SOLUTION

• Total = 65 + 126 + 135 + 148 + 165 + 95 = 734

• Average = 734 ÷ 6 = 122.333… ≈ 122.33.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Pair for easy sums: (65 + 135) + (126 + 148) + (165 + 95) = 200 + 274 + 260 = 734, then ÷6 = 122.33.

NOTE

• Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Number of observations).

question:
The pie chart given below shows the quantity of milk sold by 6 shops. The data is presented in the terms of percent.

What is the total central angle (in degrees) formed by the sectors of P and T?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 144.

GIVEN

• P = 10%, T = 30% (percent share of milk sold)

SOLUTION

• Combined percent of P and T = 10% + 30% = 40%

• Central angle = 40% of 360° = (40 ÷ 100) × 360 = 144°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Each 1% of a pie = 3.6°. So 40% × 3.6 = 144° directly.

NOTE

• In a percentage pie chart, central angle of a sector = (percentage ÷ 100) × 360°.

question:
The pie chart given below shows the number of players participated in 6 tournaments. The data is presented in the terms of degrees.

Average number of players participated in A, B and F = 80.

Total number of players participated in C and D are what percent of total number of players participated in the given 6 tournaments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 50%.

GIVEN

• Central angles: A = 54°, B = 36°, C = 108°, D = 72°, E = 60°, F = 30° (total = 360°)

SOLUTION

• Angle for C and D = 108° + 72° = 180°

• Required percent = (180° ÷ 360°) × 100 = 50%.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Percentage of any sector = (its degrees ÷ 360) × 100. Here (180 ÷ 360) × 100 = 50%; the given average of A, B, F is a distractor not needed.

NOTE

• In a degree pie chart, share of a sector = (sector angle ÷ 360°) × 100%.

question:
The bar graph given below shows the rainfall (in mm) received by the given 5 cities in a month.

What is the total rainfall (in mm) received by the B, D and E?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 235.

GIVEN

• Rainfall (mm): A = 60, B = 90, C = 75, D = 65, E = 80

SOLUTION

• Total for B, D and E = 90 + 65 + 80

• = 155 + 80 = 235 mm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Only pick the three needed bars (B, D, E) and add; ignore A and C. 90 + 80 = 170, + 65 = 235.

NOTE

• In bar graphs, the height of each bar is read directly from the value labels; sum only the asked categories.

question: A sum of money is to be distributed among P, Q, R, and S in the proportion 5:2:4:3. If R gets Rs.1000 more than S, what is the total amount of money?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. Rs.14000.

GIVEN

• P : Q : R : S = 5 : 2 : 4 : 3; R gets Rs.1000 more than S

SOLUTION

• Difference between R and S = 4 − 3 = 1 part = Rs.1000, so 1 part = Rs.1000

• Total parts = 5 + 2 + 4 + 3 = 14

• Total money = 14 × 1000 = Rs.14000.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The gap in ratio units directly equals the money gap: 1 unit = Rs.1000, so total = (sum of ratio units) × 1000 = 14 × 1000.

NOTE

• When quantities are in ratio a:b:c…, value of 1 unit = (given difference) ÷ (difference of the concerned ratio terms).

question: A chord AB of a circle is 30 cm long. If the perpendicular distance from the center to AB is 12 cm, calculate the radius of the circle. Also, determine the distance of another chord of length 24 cm from the center.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 19.2 cm, 15 cm.

GIVEN

• Chord AB = 30 cm, its distance from centre = 12 cm; second chord = 24 cm

SOLUTION

• Perpendicular from centre bisects a chord, so half of AB = 15 cm

• Radius r = √(15² + 12²) = √(225 + 144) = √369 ≈ 19.2 cm

• For the 24 cm chord, half = 12 cm; distance = √(r² − 12²) = √(369 − 144) = √225 = 15 cm. Radius ≈ 19.2 cm, distance = 15 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Notice (12, 15, 19.2) works, and for the 24 cm chord the half-chord 12 with radius² 369 gives √225 = 15 — a clean perfect square, confirming Option.

NOTE

• Radius² = (half-chord)² + (distance of chord from centre)².

question: 0.4 × 0.4 + 0.6 − 0.34 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 0.42.

GIVEN

• 0.4 × 0.4 + 0.6 − 0.34

SOLUTION

• Multiply first: 0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16

• 0.16 + 0.6 − 0.34 = 0.76 − 0.34 = 0.42.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Do the product (0.16) before adding/subtracting; then 0.16 + 0.6 = 0.76, minus 0.34 = 0.42.

NOTE

• 0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16 (multiply 4×4 = 16, then place two decimal digits). BODMAS keeps multiplication ahead of ±.

question: The product of the three consecutive odd numbers is 315. What is the sum of the largest and the smallest of the three numbers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 14.

GIVEN

• Product of three consecutive odd numbers = 315

SOLUTION

• Cube root of 315 ≈ 6.8, so numbers are near 7: try 5, 7, 9

• 5 × 7 × 9 = 315 ✓

• Sum of largest and smallest = 9 + 5 = 14.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The middle number ≈ cube root of the product (∛315 ≈ 6.8 → 7). Then largest + smallest = 2 × middle = 2 × 7 = 14.

NOTE

• For three numbers in AP, the middle term is their average; largest + smallest = 2 × middle.

question: How many numbers among 9003, 6012, 3330, 1001 are divisible by 3?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• Numbers: 9003, 6012, 3330, 1001

SOLUTION

• 9003 → 9+0+0+3 = 12, divisible by 3 ✓

• 6012 → 6+0+1+2 = 9, divisible by 3 ✓

• 3330 → 3+3+3+0 = 9, divisible by 3 ✓

• 1001 → 1+0+0+1 = 2, not divisible ✗. So 3 numbers are divisible by 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just add the digits of each number; if the digit sum is a multiple of 3, the number is divisible by 3.

NOTE

• Divisibility by 3: the sum of the digits must be divisible by 3.

question: 47P5 is divisible by 3. What is the value of P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5.

GIVEN

• 47P5 is divisible by 3

SOLUTION

• Digit sum = 4 + 7 + P + 5 = 16 + P must be divisible by 3

• From options: P = 5 → 16 + 5 = 21, which is divisible by 3 ✓ (3→19, 7→23, 9→25 are not). So P = 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 16 + P must be a multiple of 3; nearest multiple above 16 is 21, so P = 21 − 16 = 5.

NOTE

• A number is divisible by 3 when the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

question: Average of first ‘N’ odd natural numbers is 21. What is the value of ‘N’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 21.

GIVEN

• Average of first N odd natural numbers = 21

SOLUTION

• Sum of first N odd numbers = N²; Average = N² ÷ N = N

• So average = N = 21.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The average of the first N odd numbers is always N itself, so N equals the given average, 21.

NOTE

• Sum of first N odd natural numbers = N², hence their average = N.

question: Two straight lines CD and AB cut each other at point O. Angle AOD = 80 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle AOC?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 100.

GIVEN

• Lines AB and CD intersect at O; angle AOD = 80°

SOLUTION

• AOC and AOD are angles on a straight line CD (linear pair), so they add to 180°

• angle AOC = 180° − 80° = 100°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• AOD and AOC sit on straight line COD; subtract from 180°: 180 − 80 = 100.

NOTE

• Angles forming a linear pair (on a straight line) are supplementary and sum to 180°.

question: What will be the average of all the odd natural numbers between 8 and 30?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 19.

GIVEN

• Odd natural numbers between 8 and 30

SOLUTION

• They are 9, 11, 13, …, 29 (an evenly spaced set)

• Average = (first + last) ÷ 2 = (9 + 29) ÷ 2 = 38 ÷ 2 = 19.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For consecutive/evenly spaced numbers, average = (smallest + largest) ÷ 2 = (9 + 29)/2 = 19.

NOTE

• The mean of any arithmetic progression equals the average of its first and last terms.

question: In the given figure, angle ABC = 70 degrees. Angle AEF = 50 degrees. Angle CDE = 45 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle ACD?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 85.

GIVEN

• angle ABC = 70°, angle AEF = 50°, angle CDE = 45°

SOLUTION

• Lines AC and FD cross at E, so angle CED = angle AEF = 50° (vertically opposite)

• In triangle CED: angle DCE = 180° − angle CED − angle CDE = 180° − 50° − 45° = 85°

• angle ACD is the same as angle DCE, so angle ACD = 85°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• angle ACD is the exterior angle of triangle CED at C: exterior angle = 180° − (opposite two) = 180° − (50° + 45°) = 85°. The 70° is a distractor.

NOTE

• Vertically opposite angles are equal, and the three angles of a triangle sum to 180°.

question: In the given figure, AB is parallel to CD. Angle PAB = 70 degrees and angle APC = 30 degrees. What is the value (in degrees) of angle DCP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 100.

GIVEN

• AB ∥ CD, angle PAB = 70°, angle APC = 30°

SOLUTION

• Draw a line through P parallel to AB and CD. It splits angle APC so that the part next to A equals angle PAB = 70° (alternate angles) and the part next to C equals angle DCP (alternate angles).

• Since angle APC = 30° here measures beyond, angle DCP = angle PAB + angle APC = 70° + 30° = 100°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• With AB ∥ CD, the bend angle at C equals the sum of the two given angles: angle DCP = angle PAB + angle APC = 70 + 30 = 100°.

NOTE

• Drawing an auxiliary line parallel to two given parallels through the vertex converts a 'zig-zag' angle into a sum of alternate angles.
